key_insight: VideoDetective jointly reasons about extrinsic query-to-segment relevance and intrinsic inter-segment affinity to locate sparse, informative clips in long videos—enabling MLLMs to focus on true "clues" within limited context windows.
problem_solved: How to find and prioritize sparse, query-relevant segments in very long videos while accounting for the video's internal structure and varying segment relevance so MLLMs can efficiently and accurately reason.
method: Compute extrinsic relevance: score segments by how directly they match the input query (query-to-segment relevance).
Model intrinsic structure: build an inter-segment affinity graph to capture temporal/semantic relations and propagate relevance across segments.
Fuse signals and select clues: combine extrinsic and intrinsic scores to pick compact, high-value segments for downstream MLLM reasoning (efficient clue hunting).
impact: Improves accuracy and efficiency of long-video QA, retrieval, and reasoning by selecting fewer but more informative clips, making multimodal LLMs practical on long-form content and easier to interpret.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram with two parallel streams (query relevance and inter-segment affinity) that merge into a selection module feeding an MLLM.
Video timeline heatmap showing original long video with highlighted selected "clue" segments.
Affinity graph visualization (nodes = segments, edges = affinities) illustrating propagation of relevance and clustering of related clips.
Bar/chart comparing selection efficiency (fewer frames), model accuracy, and compute/time vs baseline methods.
paper_title: VideoDetective: Clue Hunting via both Extrinsic Query and Intrinsic Relevance for Long Video Understanding
paper_authors: Ruoliu Yang, Chu Wu, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Chaoyou Fu
